newsitem.title: USA: GM, NBC, Olympic officials set to announce sponsorship.
newsitem.headline: GM, NBC, Olympic officials set to announce sponsorship.

text.p: General Motors Corp., NBC Inc. and the United States Olympic Committee were set to formally announce details Wednesday of what they described as an unprecedented sports sponsorship deal.

Although the companies have declined to release specifics, the world's largest automaker has bought the rights to be the sole automotive sponsor for the U.S. Olympics through the year 2008, sources close to GM and industry sources said.
"GM will be the exclusive automotive sponsor for the U.S. Olympics through 2008, and is the official sponsor of the 2002 winter games in Salt Lake City," said a source close to GM.
Sources said the total value of the deal, which represents a major move by GM to boost its brand awareness on a global basis, could be worth up to $1 billion.
NBC, a unit of General Electric Co., has broadcast rights to the Olympics, beginning with the 2000 Summer Olympics in Sydney, Australia, through 2008.
The GM deal would be the first under a new approach, with the USOC and NBC working jointly to enlist corporations for both Olympic sponsorship and TV advertising.

The Wall Street Journal reported Tuesday that GM would spend about $700 million for sponsorship-rights fees and television advertising. Another $300 million would be spent on Olympics-related marketing, the paper reported.
GM's agreement would represent the largest sports sponsorship to date, according to the paper.

One advertising source said that it was realistic for GM to spend $700 million for sponsorship and TV advertising alone. "It's a nice round number for domestic auto exclusivity for five Olympics," said the source, who asked not to be named.
The 2002 Winter Games in Salt Lake City is considered the "crown jewel," and is considered a more expensive advertising vehicle, advertising experts said.
Meantime, Lucent Technologies Inc., Xerox Corp., and UAL Corp. all said they were in talks with the USOC about being sponsors. A Home Depot Inc. spokesman said it was considering a sponsorship.
Anheuser-Busch Cos. Inc. was near an agreement to be the official beer sponsor, according to the Journal. A company spokesman was not available to comment.
